claims.text: The baseline consists of an elemental Cr coating deposited directly on Zircaloy cladding.
Nitriding Zircaloy in a controlled N2/H2 atmosphere at approximately 600 °C can form a uniform approximately 100 nm ZrN interlayer.
Physical vapor deposition can be used to deposit the coating after formation of the interlayer.
The required structural mediator is a continuous, defect-free ZrN layer between Zircaloy and Cr.
ZrN has high thermodynamic stability under the proposed service conditions.
ZrN has sufficiently low atomic diffusivity to function as a Cr–Zr diffusion barrier.
The ZrN interlayer impedes migration of both Cr and Zr species.
Suppressing Cr and Zr migration prevents the elevated-temperature interdiffusion-driven degradation of the Cr coating.
A Cr coating deposited directly on Zircaloy is susceptible to premature failure from excessive Cr–Zr interdiffusion under accident-relevant high-temperature conditions.
Relative to the direct Cr-coated control, the ZrN interlayer will significantly reduce or virtually eliminate Cr–Zr interdiffusion during steam exposure at up to 1200 °C for approximately 30 minutes.
The ZrN interlayer will preserve the protective and corrosion-resistant performance of the Cr coating in approximately 300 °C subcritical water.
The intervention is effective during normal operation in approximately 300 °C subcritical water.
The intervention remains effective during short-term steam exposure at up to 1200 °C for approximately 30 minutes.
Variability in nitriding can produce localized defects that cause failure of the diffusion barrier.
SEM-EDX can map elemental distributions and quantify Cr–Zr interdiffusion after exposure.
XRD and BSE imaging can detect interfacial phase changes and assess microstructural integrity.
Interdiffusion comparable to that in the direct Cr-coated control, or observable interfacial degradation, is designated as a falsifying outcome.
Failure of the ZrN layer during thermal exposure is designated as a falsifying outcome.
